name: Zapotec
desc: The 'Cloud People' of the Oaxaca valley, who levelled a mountain top to build Monte Albán, carved some of the earliest writing and calendar signs of Mesoamerica, watered their fields from pots and little canals, and dyed cloth red with cochineal insects.
source: Excavations at San José Mogote and Monte Albán (Alfonso Caso from 1931; Kent Flannery and Joyce Marcus)

cautious: carried water to the maize in pots from the shallow wells all summer
devout: burned copal to the rain god on the mountain top
gluttonous: scraped enough red insects from the cactus to dye a whole cloak

inventions.name: Pot Irrigation and Canals
inventions.source: Oaxacan farmers watered maize from shallow wells by pot, and built small canals such as those of Hierve el Agua (c. 300 BCE)
inventions.desc: Shallow wells beside the fields and pots to carry water to each plant, and little canals on the slopes: farm plots yield 20% more.

inventions.name: The 260-Day Count
inventions.source: Carved stones at San José Mogote and Monte Albán carry some of the oldest Mesoamerican calendar signs and glyphs
inventions.desc: Twenty day-signs turning with thirteen numbers, so every day has a name and every child is named for the day of birth: a little more lore, rites bring 5% more devotion.
inventions.hint: Needs the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and rites.

inventions.name: City on the Mountain
inventions.source: Monte Albán was founded around 500 BCE on a levelled ridge 400 m above the valley floor
inventions.desc: A mountain top cut flat for plazas and temples, looking down on three valleys: +2 defence, people see much farther.
inventions.hint: Needs Polished Stone Tools and the Tribe & Agrarian Era.

inventions.name: Cochineal Red
inventions.source: Cochineal insects, raised on nopal cactus in Oaxaca, give the brightest red dye; after 1500 it became Mexico's second export after silver
inventions.desc: Tiny white insects scraped from the cactus and crushed into a deep red: +3 mood.

foods.name: Tortillas and Beans
foods.source: Clay griddles (comales) for tortillas appear in Oaxaca by about 700 BCE
foods.desc: Flat maize cakes cooked on a clay griddle, eaten with black beans: hunger grows 12% slower.

foods.name: Toasted Grasshoppers
foods.source: Chapulines, toasted grasshoppers, have been eaten in Oaxaca since long before the Spanish came
foods.desc: Grasshoppers from the maize fields, toasted with chilli and lime: hunger grows 5% slower, +1 mood.

finds.name: Nopal Cactus
finds.desc: Flat-padded cactus with sweet red fruit; tiny red-blooded insects live on it.

finds.name: Wild Beans
finds.desc: Climbing beans of the valley edge, one of the three sisters with maize and squash.

people.name: Nine Water
people.desc: Named for the day of water, she has never let a field go dry.
memory: found water three spans under the valley floor

people.name: One Monkey
people.desc: Born on the day of the monkey, patron of artists, he carves the day signs.
memory: carved a captive's name and his day sign on a stone

people.name: The Danzantes
people.source: Over 300 carved stone slabs of naked figures in twisted poses, probably slain captives, on Building L at Monte Albán
people.desc: Hundreds of carved figures once called 'dancers'; most now think they show enemies defeated by the first rulers of Monte Albán.

people.name: Cocijo
people.source: Zapotec funerary urns show Cocijo with a forked tongue and a lightning headdress
people.desc: The rain god of the Zapotec, whose face, with its split serpent's tongue, looks out from the urns placed in every tomb.

people.name: Ocelotl
people.source: The Lápida de Bazán and carvings at Monte Albán show envoys from Teotihuacan; there was a Oaxacan neighbourhood at Teotihuacan
people.text: an envoy from the great city in the north, with a tasselled headdress and an offer of friendship.
memory: walked for a month from the city of the pyramids
people.desc: A diplomat from Teotihuacan, of the kind carved at Monte Albán; the game names him 'Jaguar' in Nahuatl.

people.name: Thirteen Lightning
people.label: Thirteen Lightning, Voice of Cocijo
people.desc: When she calls, the rain comes. Lore 8.

people.name: One Earthquake
people.label: One Earthquake, Founder of the Mountain City
people.desc: He levels a mountain to build a city. Crafting 8, Combat 5.

people.name: Eight Jaguar
people.label: Eight Jaguar, Taker of Captives
people.desc: No warrior of the valley can stand against him. Combat 8.

events.title: A City on the Mountain Top
events.source: Around 500 BCE the people of San José Mogote and other valley towns moved together to found Monte Albán
events.text: The valley towns keep raiding one another. The chief proposes that they all move together to the mountain in the middle of the valley, level its top, and build one city.

options.label: Build on the mountain

do.feat: Founded a city on the mountain top

options.result: The mountain top is cut flat, stone by stone. From the new plaza, all three valleys can be seen.

options.label: Each town for itself
options.result: The towns keep their walls, and their quarrels.

events.title: Cocijo Holds Back the Rain
events.text: The maize is withering. The priests say Cocijo is angry and must be given copal, quail and jade on the mountain top.

options.label: Make the offerings
options.result: Smoke rises from the mountain. Lightning flickers over the hills that night.

options.label: Carry water by pot
options.result: Everyone carries water from the wells. Sore backs, but the maize lives.

events.title: Carve the Defeated
events.text: After a victory, the chief wants the defeated enemy chiefs carved in stone on the temple wall, each with his name and the day of his defeat.

options.label: Carve them
options.result: Row upon row of stone figures line the wall, and the valley towns take note.

options.label: Make peace with them
options.result: The defeated chiefs are sent home with gifts.

tales.name: The Cloud People
tales.source: Zapotec tradition records that their ancestors were born from clouds, trees and rocks
tales.text: Our first ancestors did not come from another land. They were born from the clouds over the mountains, and from the great trees and rocks of this valley. That is why we are called the Cloud People, and why, when we die, we go back to the clouds.

tales.name: Why Children Are Named for Their Day
tales.text: Every day has its own sign and number, and its own luck. A child born on Seven Deer will be gentle and quick; one born on Two Flint must be guarded against quarrels. So we name our children for their day, to know them and to help them.
tales.moral: each day has its own gift

tales.name: The Red Blood of the Cactus
tales.source: A story made up around cochineal
tales.text: A girl pricked her finger on a cactus and squeezed out a white bug, and her hand turned red as fire. She dyed her shawl and wore it to the market, and everyone wanted one. That is how the cactus taught us that the smallest creature can carry the brightest colour.

tales.name: The Maize Harvest Dance
tales.source: A story made up around the harvest festivals of Oaxaca
tales.text: When the maize is in, every village of the valley climbs to the mountain city with its best dancers and its first ears of corn. Each village dances in turn in the great plaza, and each gives a gift to the others.
